text.title: Hidden Tech Debt Trace Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules for tracing the debt a green CI run hides: skipped and uncollected tests, non-specced mocks, assertion-free tests, LLM copy-paste, single-implementer abstractions, type-suppression drift. Each rule names the scan and the threshold that turns a count into a finding.

rule.statement: The report MUST list every skipped test with its reason string, and record collected-vs-executed counts per suite. Scan for `@pytest.mark.skip`, `pytest.skip(`, `@unittest.skip`, `t.Skip(`, `xit(`, `.skip(`, `.todo(`. A suite run under Jest `--passWithNoTests`, or a pytest call whose exit code 5 is swallowed by `|| true`, is recorded as a severity-high finding — never as a pass.

rationale.source: pytest exit-code table (5 = no tests collected); Jest CLI --passWithNoTests

rule.rationale: A renamed directory or one broken import makes the collector find zero tests. With `--passWithNoTests` or a swallowed exit 5 the job returns 0, so the dashboard stays green while nothing is verified at all. Skips are the same failure at smaller radius: the count is printed, and nothing reads it.

rule.statement: Every `unittest.mock.patch` or `Mock()` without `autospec=True`, `spec=` or `spec_set=` counts as a debt item. Report, per test module, the ratio of `patch(` occurrences to `autospec=True` occurrences.
rule.rationale: A bare `Mock` answers to any attribute name and any call signature. Rename the production method, add a required argument, or delete it, and `m.old_name.assert_called_once_with(...)` still passes against the phantom attribute — the test now proves only that the test file is internally consistent.

rule.statement: Any test function whose body contains zero assertions (no `assert`, no `expect(`, no `require.`, no `t.Error`) MUST appear in the findings list. Tests whose only assertion is a call-count check on a non-specced mock are classified separately as `mock-only` and summed into the mock-only coverage figure.
rule.rationale: Line coverage records that a line executed, not that its result was checked. A test that calls the function and asserts nothing raises the coverage percentage by exactly as much as a real test does, so the coverage number cannot separate the two — only an assertion scan can.

rule.statement: Copy-paste debt MUST be measured by a named detector at a stated threshold — `jscpd --min-tokens 50`, or PMD CPD `--minimum-tokens 100` — and reported as a delta against the same command run at a pre-AI-adoption commit SHA recorded in the artefact. An absolute duplication percentage with no baseline SHA is rejected.

rationale.source: jscpd / PMD Copy-Paste Detector — token-based clone detection

rule.rationale: Every codebase has a nonzero duplication floor from generated files and boilerplate, so an absolute figure carries no verdict. LLM-assisted editing raises duplication by re-emitting a near-identical block instead of extracting it, and that shows up only as a slope between two commits.

rule.statement: Every interface, ABC, `Protocol`, or strategy/factory class with exactly one implementer AND no call site outside its own module MUST be listed as a candidate hallucinated abstraction, with implementer count and external call-site count recorded per entry.

rationale.source: Speculative generality code smell — Fowler, Refactoring (2nd ed.)

rule.rationale: A model asked for "a clean, extensible design" emits the extension point together with the single concrete case, because that shape dominates its training data. The indirection then costs a hop on every read and every debug session while buying no substitution that anything performs.

rule.statement: Record per-KLOC counts of `# type: ignore`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `as any`, `eslint-disable` and `# noqa`, plus the count of suppressions that are no longer needed, taken from `mypy --warn-unused-ignores` and from the TypeScript compiler's report on unused `@ts-expect-error`.
rule.rationale: A suppression silences the checker on that line permanently — including for errors introduced there later — so the type system stops guarding the line rather than guarding it with one documented exception. Unused suppressions are the measurable tail: they prove the marker was added to make a run go green, not to describe a real limitation.

rule.statement: Skip when ANY holds: (a) no AI-assisted commits in the trailing 3 months — use the generic tech-debt methodology, (b) repository younger than 1 month, where finding rate does not repay scan cost, (c) no test suite exists, in which case the finding is "no tests", not a debt trace, (d) no coverage or CI history on the default branch to compare against.
rule.rationale: Every rule above is a delta or a ratio against a baseline. With no baseline commit, no suite and no AI-authored change set, the scans return counts that cannot be read as findings, and the report degrades into numbers nobody can act on.
